Hi team —

SAST/DAST summary (high level):
- SAST: Primary tooling: Semgrep + internal static analyzers during CI. We run rule suites per service; weekly scheduled scans for monorepo components, per-pull-request scans for feature branches. Typical false-positive rate after filters: ~8-12% (depends on rule set). Findings are triaged into JIRA (project RED-SV) and tagged by severity (low/med/high/critical).
- DAST: Periodic dynamic scans using a mix of OWASP ZAP and custom black-box harnesses for public endpoints. Full DAST for customer-facing endpoints runs monthly; targeted runs for high-risk services on-demand.
- Mapping: All SAST/DAST alerts create JIRA issues with vulnerability metadata (CWE, scanner, raw output). Severity tuning is maintained by the AppSec triage board (me + 2 rotation engineers).

SBOMs and dependency hygiene:
- We generate SBOMs as part of the build pipeline (syft-based generator) for all actively maintained services. SBOM snapshots are stored in our artifact registry and rotated monthly.
- Known gap: several legacy on-prem installers still have manual SBOM assembly pending; we flag those in the snapshot.

Attached artifacts: sast-dast_results_20261001.csv (filtered export), sbom_snapshot_20260930.json

If Bluefield needs the raw scanner output for a specific service, tell me which service name and I'll include it.

-Neha

Hi — pen test and patch SLA notes below. I’ve attached the executive summary PDF and a CSV with our published patch SLA table.

Penetration testing:
- Last full pen test: 2026-09-20, performed by RedOak Security (third-party). Scope: hosted API endpoints + console. Executive summary attached (pen_test_exec_summary_20260920.pdf).
- Findings: 0 open criticals; 2 high findings (one mitigated, one pending verification). All medium/low items are triaged and scheduled into the next two sprint cycles. We maintain evidence artifacts for confirmed fixes.

Patch SLA (published targets):
- Critical (hosted): initial mitigation/temporary patch within 48 hours; full remediation/validated fix within 14 days (depends on complexity).
- Critical (private/on-prem): emergency fix coordination target 72 hours for a recommended mitigation; final remediation timeline negotiated case-by-case — default contract baseline 30 days.
- High: fix within 30 days; Medium/Low: scheduled per normal backlog (60–90 days).

Escalation & contact: For production-detected vulnerabilities, our incident triage is handled by the Security Operations Pager rotation. Primary escalation: security_oncall@redwood.com (24x7). For account-level coordination we use account-security@redwood.com (SLA response within 4 business hours).

Attachments: pen_test_exec_summary_20260920.pdf, patch_sla_table.csv

—Marcus

- Escalation: security_oncall@redwood.com (24x7) for operational emergencies; account-security@redwood.com for account coordination (4 business hour SLA).
